teams.heading: Mesake Vocevoce sent off for 10 minutes as Fiji lost to France
teams.body: Fiji were left a man light in Lyon: Islands Business's Alipate Pareti reports that Mesake Vocevoce was sent off for 10 minutes for collapsing a driving maul, and the Flying Fijians backpedalled as France's forwards pressed on. Pareti also notes that Vinaya Habosi was playing inside centre for the first time and that Fiji won some lineout battles, but Pareti argues they should have contested France's lineouts to stop the mauls forming.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item about Fiji's own side with a new match detail (the sending-off) not in the earlier editions.

teams.heading: Alex Mitchell has hamstring operation and could miss Six Nations
teams.body: England scrum-half Alex Mitchell has had surgery in Finland to fix recurring hamstring problems, after four injuries this year. The 29-year-old was England head coach Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season. He could miss next year's Six Nations, as an estimated four-month rehabilitation would only give him a chance at England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland. Any setback would leave him only pre-tournament friendlies before the Rugby World Cup. His latest injury had already ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign.

lead.why: A fresh England injury and surgery story that has not been reported in an earlier edition, and it matters beyond this weekend's match.

teams.heading: Kolisi says history gives Springboks no edge at Stade de France
teams.body: Siya Kolisi, the Springboks captain, has dismissed any psychological edge from history ahead of Friday's clash at the Stade de France. 'What happened last year is gone,' Kolisi said on Thursday, after winning the 2025 meeting 32-17. He said the group has changed and that they 'don't get stuck on things that have happened before.' France, by contrast, have beaten South Africa once in their past 10 meetings, in Marseille in 2022.

teams.heading: James McNabney poised for Ireland debut off the bench against Fiji
teams.body: Ulster's James McNabney has been named among the replacements for Saturday's clash with Fiji at the Aviva Stadium, with a first cap on the cards if he is called on. The 23-year-old has started just one game for Ulster this season after an anterior cruciate ligament injury forced him to miss the entire 2025-26 campaign. Ireland head coach Andy Farrell called his rise "phenomenal".

lead.why: A fresh BBC debut angle on the Fiji team news, rather than a restatement of the captaincy and seven-change story already published.

teams.heading: Italy visit Gaslini hospital and meet fans during Genoa build-up
teams.body: Italy's delegation visited Genoa's Ospedale Gaslini on Thursday, meeting young patients and their families. Today brings a Captain's Run at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, a press conference for the captain, a photo shoot with the Canile Monte Contessa animal shelter and a meeting with supporters at the Macron Store on via Canevari. The day closes with an awards evening for Ligurian rugby, organised by the Federazione Italiana Rugby and CUS Genova, followed by the Committee Dinner.

lead.why: It is the only new Italy item not already covered by the reported team selection or the Quesada press-conference quotes.

teams.heading: Tuipulotu's schoolmate Jacob Elordi ended rugby after breaking his back at 16
teams.body: Ahead of the Australia Test, talkSPORT reports that Scotland international Sione Tuipulotu shared a school team at St Kevin's College in Melbourne with actor Jacob Elordi. Elordi told the Hollywood Reporter in January that he broke his back at 16 after lifting weights too early and squatting wrong, then went into a tackle, and a rugby coach had asked him to choose between sport and drama. Scotland team-mate Blair Kinghorn says Tuipulotu still claims he is the school's most famous former pupil.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and it concerns Scotland's Sione Tuipulotu ahead of the Australia Test.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy admits Wales are heavily reliant on Tomos Williams
teams.body: Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams played the full 80 minutes against Japan, the fifth time under head coach Steve Tandy that he has not been replaced. Williams has averaged around 74 minutes across those 12 Tests under Tandy, while Ospreys pair Kieran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams have combined for just 48 minutes off the bench. Hardy has been ruled out for the season, and uncapped Dragons half-back Che Hope has joined three-cap Morgan-Williams in the squad.

lead.why: A new Tandy admission about Wales's scrum-half dependence is a fresh, Wales-specific story, unlike the Basham and Wainwright team news already run.

teams.heading: Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada expects Pumas to come out swinging in Genoa
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has given his read on the Pumas ahead of Saturday's match in Genoa. He says Argentina arrive with more defeats than they are used to, have taken criticism and have voiced their own disappointment. Italy have prepared on the contest, defence and discipline, Quesada said, and he expects "Mi immagino un’Argentina all’arrembaggio e che metterà tutta la sua aggressività fin dal primo minuto." He also flagged the aerial game the Pumas use a lot.

lead.why: It is the freshest item in the pack and is about Argentina's mood and reputation, which the Pumas' own edition can use, and it is not a repeat of the selection or call-up already published.

teams.heading: Wallabies scrum-half Ryan Lonergan defends Joseph Suaalii after Chris Ashton's criticism
teams.body: Scrum-half Ryan Lonergan has backed Joseph Suaalii after the winger drew criticism following Australia's 45-22 loss to England at Twickenham. Lonergan told reporters Suaalii was "a great team-mate, great athlete" and said the back three were not getting opportunities through any fault of their own. Former England winger Chris Ashton had questioned whether the ex-rugby league star looked like a union international. Lonergan also said collisions were the main point from the Wallabies' defensive review ahead of Sunday's Murrayfield test against Scotland.

lead.why: The only NEW item (#1) is about Scotland, and #4 has already run today, so this Suaalii piece is the freshest Australia story left.

teams.heading: Miu Austin Moriyama returns home injured; Faulua Makisi called up
teams.body: Japan have made two mid-week changes ahead of Saturday's match at Twickenham. Miu Austin Moriyama and Inoke Brua have returned home injured, and Faulua Makisi of Kubota Spears Funabashi/Tokyo Bay and Jone Naikabra of Toshiba Brave Lupus Musashi have been called up to replace them. Rinku Tokito of Toshiba Brave Lupus Musashi is set to make his debut on the left wing, with Riku Kitahara keeping the No. 10 jersey and earning his second cap.

lead.why: Both NEW items are about England, not Japan, so the lead falls back to #3 because it carries the only Japan-specific squad news on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names forward-heavy six-two bench split for Wales Test
teams.body: New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has finally gambled on a bench heavy with forwards, after teasing it all year, for Saturday's Nations Championship Test in Cardiff. Leicester Fainga'anuku is listed as a loose forward but is a centre or winger by trade, and he has played openside flanker for Toulon and the Crusaders. Ian Foster trialled the split just once, in the 35-7 loss to the Springboks at Twickenham before the World Cup, while Scott Robertson never tried it.

lead.why: A new team-selection story about New Zealand's bench, distinct from the already-reported captaincy news.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names Wilco Louw at tighthead in two-change Springbok side
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has retained most of the 23 that scored 66 points against Italy, with Wilco Louw in at tighthead. France, by contrast, go into Friday's round-five clash without Romain Ntamack, Matthieu Jalibert, Antoine Hastoy or Thomas Ramos. The Boks are four from four in the Nations Championship, top of the southern group on points difference, and chasing a place in the Twickenham final on 29 November.
